result.reason: Clarity: A uses bolded section headers and short single-topic paragraphs suited to phone reading, and translates jargon (explains the index composition, glosses the duration shortening as bonds maturing sooner, near when she needs the money). It also flags that only half the 2026 distribution has been paid and that the firm will follow up on the rest. B is four dense blocks with no headings, opens with a sentence stacking strategy, net return, fee treatment and gross return, uses equities/fixed income/gross-of-fees/duration/since inception unglossed, and merges distribution figures into a bond-strategy paragraph. Tone: A is warm and plain, presents the fee increase cause-first and explicitly invites questions about it. B misfires twice: "We are pleased to report" attached to a defensive change in a quarter that trailed its index, and the florid "navigate this important chapter of your financial life" to a bereaved beneficiary, which cuts against the plain-English tone note. A's only tone flaw is the impersonal "Dear Castellanos-Weir Household" where B correctly uses "Dear Ines" — a one-line fix against B's structural problems. Length was not a factor; the letters are comparable in size and A wins on organization, not volume.
